reviewer: fresh-context-adversary (independent file verification against real codebase, post scope-pivot)
summary: The scope pivot's DIAGNOSIS is correct and independently confirmed: `grep -n '"ig-account-create"' ~/anicca/skills/registry.json` genuinely returns 0 matches, and clip-cli.sh's real STARTUP string (line 18) genuinely instructs claude-p to run run.sh/monitor.sh only, never mentioning self-provisioning an account. The gap Dais identified is real, not imagined. However, the PRESCRIBED FIX for the genesis-loop half of REQ-102(a) does not work, and this is not a nitpick — it is the same class of load-bearing mechanism error that failed iteration-1 (FIND-001, wrong env-propagation file). Direct evidence: `~/anicca/runtime/loop/run-skill.mjs:105-112`'s `resolveSkillPath()` hardcodes the entrypoint filename as the literal string 'run.sh' and never reads `registry.slots[slot].entrypoint` at all -- across the entire repo that field is read in exactly one place (`install.sh:123`), purely for a human-facing echo message about 'declared' (not-yet-live) slots, never for actual invocation. Separately, ig-account-create has no run.sh anywhere (its scripts/ dir holds only cdp.py/cdp_incognito.py/ig_dob.py/read_otp.py/read_sms_otp.py/setup_profile.py plus SKILL.md) and lives entirely outside ~/anicca/skills/ (canonical ~/.agents/skills/ig-account-create/, symlinked into ~/.claude/skills/ and ~/.openclaw/skills/ only). Most fundamentally, ig-account-create's own documented 'Proven flow' is an inherently agent-judgment-driven procedure (pick a username until an error message clears, re-verify a field corrupted by autocomplete, choose the visible listbox among several, read Gmail OTP that sometimes lands in spam) -- exactly the kind of task this project's own memory (`feedback_warmup_two_layer_agentic_not_brittle_selectors`) says must stay agent-driven, not a fire-and-forget script `runSkill()` can spawn non-interactively and wait ~120s for. Writing a deterministic run.sh wrapper to make it 'invocable' the same way earn/clip is would require substantial new brittle-automation code, directly contradicting REQ-102's own claim of zero new signup code. REQ-102(b) (updating claude-p's STARTUP prompt) is, by contrast, genuinely sound: claude-p is a real spawned `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` CLI process (clip-cli.sh:33) with full native Skill/Read/Bash tool access, so it can actually follow ig-account-create's SKILL.md itself with real judgment, exactly as any Claude Code session can -- no registry, no run_skill, no new code needed. Because only one of the two loops can reach the described outcome, REQ-102's verification bar ('trigger a REAL wake of EITHER loop ... CONFIRM the agent itself chose to invoke ig-account-create') is not achievable as written and should commit explicitly to the claude-p path (FIND-007). Two further, more minor issues: REQ-103's agent-written account-file entry has no validation step, and the real consumer (run.sh:42-51) silently defaults a missing 'port' key to 9222 -- Dais's own daily-driver port, exactly the D-63 collision class this spec explicitly tries to avoid (FIND-008, treated as blocking given the safety stakes). And the wallet-exception reasoning cites the wrong function as precedent -- identity.mjs's assignIdentity only names an already-existing address, it does not generate a wallet -- while the actually-relevant precedent (self/spawn/scripts/gen-wallet.sh, already invoked fully autonomously by self/spawn/run.sh) shows wallet-gen has zero mechanical obstacle to being made agent-invoked too, unlike ig-account-create (FIND-009, informational, not blocking since the wallet already exists and works). REQ-104's citations (post_reel.py:117-118) and launch_clip_browser.py's existence were independently re-verified fresh and remain accurate -- the pivot rewrite did not corrupt REQ-104/105/106/107's already-PASSED technical content.
verified_accurate_claims: grep -n '"ig-account-create"' ~/anicca/skills/registry.json -> 0 matches; only "earn/clip" (line 124) is present with track/dir/entrypoint/status/owner/spec/summary fields.

clip-cli.sh's real STARTUP string (line 18) genuinely says '...only posts when ... a ready logged-in clip account in ~/.cloak/clip-accounts.json exist...' and never mentions self-provisioning an account when none exists.

clip-cli.sh:33 genuinely spawns claude-p as `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --add-dir "$HOME" -- "$STARTUP"` -- a real Claude Code CLI process with native tool access, distinct from the ClawRouter genesis loop's run_skill/registry mechanism.
resolveSkillPath() in run-skill.mjs hardcodes filename 'run.sh' and base path $ANICCA_HOME/skills/<slot>/, never reading registry.slots[slot].entrypoint.
The only repo-wide consumer of registry .entrypoint is install.sh:123, for a status!=live human-facing message only.
~/.claude/skills/ig-account-create/scripts/ contains only .py files, no run.sh; canonical location ~/.agents/skills/ig-account-create/ is outside ~/anicca/skills/.
run.sh:42-51's account-file parser: try/except silently degrades to empty list on parse error; x.get('port', 9222) silently defaults to port 9222 on a missing key.
identity.mjs's assignIdentity(address, home) takes an existing address as input and only derives+persists a display name -- confirmed it does not generate any wallet keypair.
self/spawn/scripts/gen-wallet.sh is a real, deterministic, already-existing keypair generator invoked automatically by self/spawn/run.sh with zero human/dev involvement.
post_reel.py:117 is the ev() active-handle read, :118 is `if active != a.handle:` -- re-confirmed fresh, matches REQ-104's citation exactly, unchanged by the pivot rewrite.
